payload.content: For IoT edge deployments on constrained ARM devices, MQTT has the edge on raw latency and footprint (Mosquitto runs under 2MB resident; QoS 0 publishes complete in well under a millisecond on Raspberry Pi-class hardware). NATS wins when you need both pub/sub AND request-reply in the same broker — its subject hierarchy is more expressive and JetStream gives you persistence — but it costs ~30MB of resident memory which matters on the tightest devices. Pick MQTT if pub/sub alone is sufficient and memory is tight; pick NATS when the workload needs request-reply or you have >256MB RAM to spare.
